$comment: Seed content for the Discover screen. Categories are created first (existing ones are reused by name, not duplicated). Experiences reference EXISTING place ids already in the Xano `places` table, so no new place records are created. Run with scripts/discover-seed/seed-discover.mjs — see README.md.

experiences.title: Williamsburg Night Out
experiences.description: Bowl a few frames with live music at Brooklyn Bowl, then keep the crew moving between a cozy cocktail den and a rowdy back-patio bar. Built for a group that wants dinner, drinks, and a dance floor in walking distance.

experiences.title: Ping Pong & Rooftop in Flatiron
experiences.description: Warm up over ping pong tables at SPiN, graze the food stalls at Eataly, then cap the night with skyline cocktails at 230 Fifth. An easy crowd-pleaser that scales from four to a dozen.

experiences.title: Koreatown BBQ & Karaoke
experiences.description: Grill your own Korean BBQ at Baekjeong, chase it with shaved-ice dessert, then belt it out in a private karaoke room. The classic group-dinner-to-late-night pipeline.

experiences.title: Chelsea Market Graze & Stroll
experiences.description: Split small plates across the vendors at Chelsea Market, browse the makers at Artists & Fleas, then walk it off along the High Line. Low-commitment, easy to wander, great for mixed groups.

experiences.title: Harlem Renaissance Trail
experiences.description: Trace Harlem's cultural legacy from the Studio Museum's contemporary galleries to a gospel service at Abyssinian Baptist Church, then soul food at Sylvia's. A living history of Black art and community uptown.

experiences.title: Museum Mile Afternoon
experiences.description: Pair the sprawling collections of the Met with the intimate Klimt-and-Schiele rooms of the Neue Galerie, then take a Viennese coffee break at Café Sabarsky. Two very different ways to see Old-World art on Fifth Avenue.

experiences.title: Lower East Side Immigrant Heritage
experiences.description: Step inside a preserved tenement apartment, tour the ornate Eldridge Street Synagogue, then eat like it's 1914 at Russ & Daughters. The immigrant story of the Lower East Side told through three landmarks.

experiences.title: Long Island City Art Day
experiences.description: Cross the river for cutting-edge shows at MoMA PS1, the stone-and-garden calm of the Noguchi Museum, and monumental outdoor works at Socrates Sculpture Park. A quieter, more contemporary museum day in Queens.

experiences.title: West Village Classic Evening
experiences.description: Our go-to Village night: green-market Italian at Via Carota, a nightcap at the historic White Horse Tavern, and a table at the perennially charming Little Owl. Timeless, walkable, hard to get wrong.

experiences.title: Red Hook Waterfront Day
experiences.description: A staff favorite off the beaten path: lobster rolls by the water, a legendary slice of key lime pie, and a tasting at Red Hook Winery on the pier. Cobblestones, harbor views, and no subway stop in sight.

experiences.title: Nolita Italian Icons
experiences.description: The vodka-sauce pizza at Rubirosa, a coal-oven pie at Lombardi's, and a proper espresso at Café Integral. Three Nolita institutions we send everyone to, in one short loop.

experiences.title: Greenwich Village Jazz & Bites
experiences.description: Dinner at the beloved Jack's Wife Freda, a slow coffee at century-old Cafe Reggio, then a late set at the Blue Note. Our favorite way to spend a jazz-forward night below 14th.

experiences.title: Governors Island Escape
experiences.description: A short ferry ride delivers you to car-free lawns, the panoramic climb up The Hills, and a soak with skyline views at QC NY Spa. A whole island of quiet, minutes from Lower Manhattan.

experiences.title: Fort Tryon & The Cloisters
experiences.description: Uptown and far from the crowds: medieval art and cloistered gardens at The Cloisters, wandering paths through Fort Tryon Park, and a garden-side meal at New Leaf. Manhattan at its most tranquil.

experiences.title: Secret Midtown Pocket Parks
experiences.description: Duck off the avenues into three hidden oases: the waterfall wall at Greenacre Park, the tucked-away Paley Park, and the indoor jungle of the Ford Foundation Atrium. A stealth reset in the middle of Midtown.

experiences.title: Chinatown Off the Beaten Path
experiences.description: Skip the tourist blocks for the golden Buddhas of the Mahayana Temple, the morning tai-chi and card games of Columbus Park, and a scoop at the original Chinatown Ice Cream Factory. The neighborhood locals actually use.

experiences.title: Rooftop Sunset for Two
experiences.description: Time it for golden hour: cocktails as the skyline lights up at 230 Fifth, then a candlelit table at the Refinery Rooftop. High-romance, low-effort, all views.

experiences.title: West Village Romance
experiences.description: A slow West Village evening: handmade pasta at Via Carota, a hidden cocktail at Employees Only, and a riverfront walk out to Pier 45 to watch the sun set over the Hudson.

experiences.title: DUMBO Waterfront Date
experiences.description: Postcard New York for two: dinner with the skyline at The River Cafe, a stroll under the Brooklyn Bridge in the park, and a nightcap at Cecconi's. Bring a camera.

experiences.title: Speakeasy Cocktail Crawl
experiences.description: For a couple who loves a secret door: start at the phone-booth entrance of PDT, move to the craft cocktails at Death & Co, and end at the hushed, hidden Angel's Share. Intimate all the way through.

experiences.title: Candlelit Williamsburg Evening
experiences.description: A relaxed Brooklyn date: a romantic pasta dinner at Misi, then low-lit cocktails in the antique-mirrored back room of Hotel Delmano. Close together, no rush.

experiences.title: East Village After Dark
experiences.description: When the night's just getting started: craft cocktails at Death & Co, a dive-bar detour to Doc Holliday's, and pierogi at Veselka whenever hunger hits — it's open till late.

experiences.title: Lower East Side Late Night
experiences.description: Live bands at Pianos, an award-winning nightcap at the no-menu Attaboy, and a pastrami sandwich at Katz's to close it out. The LES doing what it does best after midnight.

experiences.title: Bushwick Warehouse Night
experiences.description: Go big in Bushwick: circus-cabaret and a packed dance floor at House of Yes, then bar-hop between The Three Diamond Door and Lovejoys until the trains start running again.

experiences.title: Midnight Jazz in the Village
experiences.description: Chase the late sets: intimate, no-phones jazz at Smalls, a legendary basement show at the Village Vanguard, and the folk-rock history of Café Wha?. Music until the small hours.

experiences.title: Free Manhattan Green Spaces
experiences.description: Zero-dollar New York: walk the elevated gardens of the High Line, catch free programming on the lawn at Bryant Park, and people-watch at the fountain in Washington Square. All free, all day.

experiences.title: Cheap Eats Chinatown
experiences.description: Eat well for next to nothing: soup dumplings at Vanessa's, dim sum at century-old Nom Wah, and an unusual scoop at the Chinatown Ice Cream Factory. Hard to spend twenty dollars.

experiences.title: Free Art in Chelsea
experiences.description: Gallery-hop the Chelsea art scene for free — blue-chip shows at Gagosian and David Zwirner — then walk the High Line between them. World-class art, no admission.

experiences.title: Slice & Stroll in the Village
experiences.description: A classic cheap day out: browse the miles of shelves at The Strand, nurse a cappuccino at old-school Cafe Reggio, and land in Washington Square Park for the street performers. Small change, big afternoon.
